Played this game for about a year and a half. This was my first MMO and to be honest I really enjoyed it. I've yet to play another MMO that has quite captured me the way this game did.

The graphic design, the effects, the monsters and the gripping storyline all tie this beatuifully made game together. The game is also quite long, as there is A LOT to do, there are a multitude of battle, crafting and gathering classes that you can level individually, as well as trade with others who have already mastered a specific craft. The battle style and mechanics are very similar to WoW (or so I'm told, never played it myself).

Some of the drawbacks include, many sidequests that tend to becoms tedious, especially in the expansion where you would spend about an entire day doing side quests for a bunch of Moogles, and still not be done after about 3-4 hours. The level gap between the base game and the expansion (50-51) seems to take a lot of grinding to get past.

Regardless of the flaws however I really did enjoy my time in this game, and I enjoyed playing with my fellow guild members in our Free Company House that we saved and renovated together.

I Definitely reccomend this game for anyone who loves the Final Fantasy franchise as they will pick up on many easter eggs and references along the journey.

tldir: if you have been looking at a lot of gameplay videos and content patch trailers of FF XiV...and still wonder wether to try it or not... just do it. If any thumbnail of FF XiV immedeatly bums you out...forget this one.

Final Fantasy XIV as an MMO does not offer any new or completely ground breaking MMO RPG elements. It simply combines the ones that MMO players are already familiar with into a very solid foundation.

For casual players: There is a big world with lots to explore.A huge main story questline. Many collectibles and mini games (a pet rts game and a card game similar to ff 8 ...just to name a few). Lots of instanced encouters for PUGs (4-man dungeons, 8-man dungeons, raids.. etc). Among those there are specific boss batlles that are called "trials". Trials are simply singular bossfights
you can queue for.

For beginners: The game will have plenty of introductory quests into its specific systems. The new feature of the novice halls will also introduce every new player into their specific role in a dungeon group (dps, healer and tank)

For hardcore gamers: So far ff Xiv seems to be patcheng new content quite freqently. Each new contentpatch contains upgrade difficulty levels of older dungeons and new ones as well. The raid content also progresses steadily

I wanted, and tried really hard, to like this game but I just couldnt. I played the base game and then the next expansion - the dungeons are great and classes/profession system very good but thats were it stopped for me. The stories, that everyone raves about, bored me to absolute tears. The constant travelling for a 30 second dialogue with a NPC to progress through the story just made me so frustrated. I dont agree that theres lots to do outside the story - I found the other activities unsatisfying on the whole. And then finally theres the ridiculous little 'cute' lalafell that I just couldnt take seriously. Theres no immersion for me, the graphics are very old and tired. The community is friendly but theres almost a cult like fan base who, and I quote, are walking advertisements for the game. I just dont get the hype sorry - but each to their own.

Ironically one of the best single-player narratives I've ever had the pleasure of experiencing throughout its 4 expansions. A hard sell for those who don't take well to typical MMO-fare, but the developers have taken many steps over its brilliant history to simplify many aspects for new players, as well as improving advanced options for veterans. Absolutely love that you can be as many jobs (classes) as you want all on the same character. Also, Masayoshi Soken's music in this game can very well be considered its own genre.

The things that keep me coming back every patch though are the "meta" components of the game, namely the developers and the community. The developers are ridiculously transparent with their plans for the game, and most changes they make feel like they enhance the game, rather than dilute it. For a live-service game that you pay a monthly sub for, this inspires confidence that your time and money aren't being wasted. The community has also been ridiculously helpful, and in my ~800 hours at time of review, I haven't had a single toxic experience (YMMV).
If this game was toast, it would be a really big piece of toast that tasted good in most areas.

I've been playing Runescape for 22 years and I've tried a few other MMOs along the way like Guild Wars, Phantasy Star Online, Black Desert Online, etc. This is the first one to really grab my attention and keep me playing. I put around 40 hours into the free version of FFXIV and found myself wanting to buy the whole game. It's currently on sale for $10 or $30 with the Endwalker expansion, which is absolutely worth it, and the subscription is about the same as a Runescape membership. This game easily has hundreds of hours in the main story alone, much less all of the jobs/skills, side quests, dungeons, raids, etc. If you've been considering trying this game, there is absolutely nothing to lose in at least trying the free version. The free version is free forever up to level 70 and only really limits you from the current expansion and social/market features.

I was a massive hater the last time I wrote this review. While I still think working with the subscription service could be a PAIN IN THE ASS sometimes, it's still a very great game. I've been playing since the game was released as a solo player, and this is by far the best game to do so, the community can be very helpful to anybody of any skill level and the game itself is wonderful. I've played a lot of MMO's but this game has always had a attachment to me. Watching the game grow as well as my own character has felt like an experience not unlike live a separate adventurers life. The story is very interesting, albeit a little boring as far a ARR is concern but gets much much better as it continues. I'm sure I got more to say, but I can't really think of much beyond that. I just personally wish they're were easy ways to make money, but It's not like money is that important. As far as a subscription MMO's go, this is definitely easily one of the best.

Do NOT buy this before getting to level 60 with the demo, which is free. That's ~40-80 free hours of content, which can translate to ~3 months worth of subscription time depending on how often you play. It turns out that when you do buy it, you are locked out of that "free until level 60". People defend this by using the semantics of it being a "free trial" to get around the fact that it's a noob trap. The game is solid and otherwise not so predatory from what I've seen, but it's disappointing that it essentially punishes you for buying it too soon. I do not recommend purchasing it, at least not until you've played through the entire free trial (you may have to do some research to find it, as it seems to be intentionally hidden from this page).

My only "negative" (and its more of just an FYI/warning) is that the end game is heavily based around having a group and finding groups to do content with. There is PLENTY of end game content to do, you just cant join a matchmaking queue necessarily and quickly connect to players, its very community driven so you have to actively seek people to play it with. So, if your shy just be conscious of this. I will say, the community is very supportive (unlike a lot of other gaming communities) which is great.

Great game, The Graphics are Amazing when turned on Maximium. The voice acting is not so good but the game has loads of content, Loads of Dungeons, A Dedicated team of Devs and Customer Support, Along with the Epic storytelling of a Final Fantasy Game. Just when you think you beat the story more story and content is added. The armoury system allows for great class changing only purpose to have multiple characters is to be in multiple Free Companies (guilds). Over all this game is a must have for a great MMO and a great way for someone to start off gaming in the MMO space.

Great MMO that rose from the ashes of those before it, buying the latest expansion will always give you the previous expacs for free, along with 30 days of gametime for new accounts. The dev team are very community oriented and provide updates to feedback from the players through streams and events. The shop (in which you use actual money to buy things) is mostly used for cosmetic items and class boosts/story skips. The amount of content in this game is nearly immeasurable. While the global cooldown rate seems rather slow, once you get most of your skills onto the hotbar you may find that the reason for this is to provide some sort of rhythm to your skill usage. Which is why the beginning is such a slog and may turn away some new players, as they will not have unlocked their skills. That being said, I still recommend this to any who are in search of a newer MMORPG. I also recommend newer players to ask any current players on their friendslist for a recruitment code, as it provides an in-game item that gives XP buffs among other items. Also the music is hype as fuck dude.

There are so many dps that queues are inflated to an insane degree, 4 tanks and 4 healers? Why?

Which shouldnt be okay, thats hundreds of hours of AAR to shadowbringers, its nuts they expect people to stick around to play through it to that point with lackluster combat. Yes the writing is good, but AAR is a slog it made me just end up skipping through.
